title: Tech Note: Introduction to Project Mode
author: Rajae CHETOUANI, Quality Support Engineer, 4D Morocco
featured_technology: Source control (git) friendly plain-text project files

historical_commentary.text: Project mode, introduced starting v17 R5 and described here in its early form, has since become 4D's default and strongly recommended database architecture, with binary/.4DB Design mode now considered legacy; the note's core description of the plain-text, source-control-friendly file layout (methods, forms, catalog, users/groups, menus) remains an accurate account of how Project mode still works today, though the tooling around it (Git integration, conversion assistants) has matured significantly since 2020.
related_updates: Project mode is now 4D's default and recommended database format; binary/Design mode (.4DB) is legacy and mainly relevant only for very old databases not yet converted
4D has since released more advanced Project Mode Conversion Assistant tooling and deeper git-workflow integration than existed when this introductory note was written

The specific JSON/text file layout described (folder.json, directory.json, menu.json, catalog.4DCatalog, .4dm/.4DForm files) remains substantially the same structural approach used by Project mode today
